name: Gullstitch Sail Loft — complementary rear-left correction
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit this architectural two-view concept plate. CRITICAL: keep the ENTIRE LEFT-HAND FRONT/STREET illustration exactly unchanged: same pixels/composition, all hoist shutters, hanging sail, net gallery, gable roof, cupola, chimney, shop doorway, sign, pots and paving. Keep the same 1536x1024 canvas, ivory paper, painted warm outlines, high detail, lighting, framing and equal view scale.

Change ONLY the RIGHT-HAND building view. The current plate mistakenly shows the SAME net-gallery side in both images. The right-hand view must instead show the genuine diagonally OPPOSITE REAR-LEFT CORNER of that very same building, so the pair reveals ALL FOUR DIFFERENT FACADES, not a repeated wall.

Read the LEFT drawing as FRONT + RIGHT wall: front is the gable with the tall shuttered sail-loading opening and hoist; right wall is the long NET-DRYING GALLERY wall. For the new RIGHT drawing, turn around the building by 180 degrees: show the BACK gable and the previously unseen LEFT long wall. Keep the same orthographic 45-degree diagonal azimuth, approximately 31-degree downward elevation, no perspective convergence. In this rear-left view the BACK gable should face the viewer toward the lower-left, and the previously unseen LEFT LONG WALL should recede toward the upper-right. All verticals parallel. This is an actual rotation around a building, NOT horizontal mirroring of the front.

SPECIFIC NEW RIGHT-PANEL FACADES:
- Rear gable: same cream plaster/timber and limestone foundations, regular small teal-shuttered work windows, a plain oak service door, downpipe and small tiled shelter for a mending bench with neatly folded sailcloth and a spool of twine. No front loading shutters or front hanging sign here.
- Previously unseen LEFT long service wall: plain pale salt-worn plaster with structural timber posts, three practical teal-shuttered workshop windows across each upper level, a small narrow ground-level service door, clean gutters and a drain. A ground-floor wall-mounted narrow canvas awning shelters two rope reels, a lean mending board and a low bench. A few coastal work details, no second large upper balcony.
- The large NET-DRYING GALLERY remains ONLY on the building's RIGHT wall, which is hidden on the far side of this new view. Do NOT draw the gallery running down the newly shown long wall. At most its far-end roof edge can peek beyond the rear corner; no long hanging net balcony in the right panel.
- Preserve the SAME long rust-red tiled gable roof, same small teal roof-ridge ventilation cupola, same masonry chimney position relative to ridge and building ends as the LEFT reference. The front hoist remains on the distant hidden front gable, not moved to the back.
- Show the entire building from finial to paving, roomy paper gaps, no new people, robots, text labels, arrows or scenery.

Do not change the left image while correcting the right. Deliver one complete detailed two-view plate.
status: selected B plate in the unselected A/B/C concept pack; correction to show four facades, no runtime model or placement
